summary: The team is juggling urgent IT access recovery with finalizing the knowledge website redesign and ramping up the China-focused marketing push for Asia Star and Intelligent China, while multiple content and partnership tasks loom.
summaryDetail: Right now, the most immediate issue is the Outlook account lockout: the team must delete and re-login on all devices, check home devices, and confirm unlock status with JSB to restore email access. On the marketing front, the priority is executing the plan to push Asia Star and Intelligent China—drafting target prompts, auditing analytics for conversion tracking, and analyzing Asia Star participant profiles—while US programs (Berkeley, Columbia, Stanford) are on hold with Berkeley as a possible third priority. The knowledge website redesign is near completion: Joseph needs to share the HTML inspiration file, the team will meet for final feedback, and Joker will implement changes, with decisions to keep the centered menu, add BCI/BSI indices, and remove the video section. This week also demands progress on several content and partnership items: Julie must send Macrobond notes, follow up with LinkedIn, update invoice payment, and postpone the school PPT copy delivery; LIU Xuan should share the concept note with Shengjia; Ira and Xuan need to review the Women in Leadership Forum design; and Joseph must check on motion graphics and a stronger banner for CKGSB Monthly. Looking ahead, Julie will assess the feasibility and budget for the '48 hours inside Asia Start' video, and Ira will provide a rough estimate for a separate website, all while the team keeps the October 16 action items on track.
